clue.text: Song following less than mature north bank resident

indicators.note: less than the whole word means it falls short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: ripe, cut short by its final letter
an aria is a solo song in opera
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Someone living on the north bank of a river is described by song and maturity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' tells us the song comes after the shortened word for mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Riparian describes a creature or person living on a riverside, so used as a noun it is one who dwells there.

clue.text: See 27
Show disgust about the Queen's hairpiece

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: to puke is to vomit, a crude display of revulsion
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Someone recoils in disgust at the monarch's wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruke is a periwig, the long powdered wig worn in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.

clue.text: Run out by nut in extravagant style

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
coco is the coconut palm and its nut

explanation.surface: A batsman is dismissed thanks to some nutcase, in a showy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' simply places the nut beside the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century decorative manner, known for elaborate flourishes and excess.

clue.text: "Fall, O Simon Russell!" said 21

definitions.note: 21 is WHEELS, slang for a car

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the quoted words count for how they sound when uttered

parts.note: fall is the American autumn, and Simon Russell Beale is an English stage actor

explanation.surface: A dramatic cry of command to an actor, as if on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall gives the season, not a tumble; spoken quickly, autumn, O and the actor's surname Beale run together into one familiar word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels is informal slang for a car, and an automobile is a motor car.

clue.text: Return of a Catholic beast to a city in Poland

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the opening words are written right to left

parts.note: taken as written
RC stands for Roman Catholic
a cow is a farm beast

explanation.surface: An animal belonging to a Catholic is brought back to a Polish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'a Catholic' is turned round; the beast follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracow is the older English spelling of Krakow, the historic royal capital in southern Poland.

clue.text: Ancient road revealed in weary dig

indicators.note: what a dig turns up has been churned out of the ground, so the letters emerge in a new order

parts.note: the two words supply all eight letters

explanation.surface: Archaeologists, tired from their excavation, uncover an old track.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ridgeway is a prehistoric track running across the chalk downs of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ridgeway is often called Britain's oldest road, used since prehistoric times along the downland ridge.

clue.text: Fiddle some figures like the modern Mrs Beeton?

parts.note: to cook accounts is to falsify them
a book is a set of accounts, as in cooking the books

explanation.surface: A modern celebrity cook is accused of fiddling the accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Beeton wrote the Victorian bestseller Book of Household Management, largely recipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Beeton's famous work was a recipe manual, so her present-day equivalent would be a recipe volume; the question mark flags the loose personification.

clue.text: Electrical unit on trust up against Richard II

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from its bottom to its top

parts.note: to rely on is to trust

explanation.surface: Electrical engineering set against a medieval king.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the word for trust from bottom to top. Wat Tyler led the 1381 Peasants' Revolt against the young Richard II.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is a cryptic description: the rebel leader whose uprising was directed at King Richard the Second.

clue.text: Return of a priest to another, telling it as it was

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the opening words are written right to left

parts.note: taken as written
Rev is short for Reverend, a priest's title
picks up the previous clue: after 'to a city', this is to another city

explanation.surface: A clergyman goes back to another place, honestly reporting events.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue echoes 5 across, which ends 'to a city'; here 'to another' means to another city, giving the plain word.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is truthfulness, the quality of reporting events exactly as they happened.

clue.text: Commercial decay keeps one deft

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a commercial

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: rot is decay
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A decaying business somehow holds on to one skilful person.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit and deft are synonyms, both describing nimble skill with the hands or mind.

clue.text: Cook meal served with Italian water

indicators.note: a served dish has been prepared and dished up, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: both words are the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A chef's dinner is served alongside a glass of Italian mineral water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters belong in the mix; 'served' is what rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Como is a famous body of water in Lombardy, northern Italy.

clue.text: Author of 24 25 initially in a layer of shingle

indicators.note: in places the poet's letters inside the word for a layer

parts.note: a ply is one layer or thickness
the poem 24 25 is by Elizabeth Barrett Browning, and initially asks for her initials

explanation.surface: A poet's initials are found within a stratum of beach stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' asks for the author's initials rather than first letters of clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a beach of small rounded stones, so ground made of it is covered in pebbles.

clue.text: Support for Sir Alec from another place

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
Sir Alec Douglas-Home was British Prime Minister in 1963 and 1964

explanation.surface: Political backing for a former Prime Minister comes from somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another place' is also Commons slang for the House of Lords, where Home sat as an earl, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A second residence, such as a weekend cottage, is another place where someone lives.

clue.text: Rude fellow eating cheese — in Old English, an old pipe

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so the cheese goes within the rude fellow

parts.note: OE is the abbreviation for Old English
a boor is an ill-mannered man
Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: An oaf munches cheese and smokes an antique pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions: the cheese goes inside the rude fellow, and that goes 'in' the Old English abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe d'amore is a baroque woodwind instrument, a slightly lower oboe much used by Bach.

clue.text: Started on fish in bottom of river

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the river's bottom

parts.note: a riverbed is the bottom of a river
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: An angler began fishing at the bottom of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject or a cask is to open or begin it, so broached means started on.

clue.text: En route, incidentally

definitions.meaning: first meaning: along the road, during a journey
second meaning: a phrase introducing a passing remark

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are literal and figurative uses of the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both on the journey itself and, as an aside, by way of a passing comment.

clue.text: Note left for bird with halo

parts.note: G is a note of the musical scale
L is the abbreviation for left
the oriole is a brightly coloured songbird

explanation.surface: A note is left for a bird that wears a halo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' simply lines up the bird after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloriole is an aureole or nimbus, the ring of light painted around a holy figure's head.

clue.text: Oral with old boy network produces very blue fluid

indicators.note: a network is a mesh of criss-crossed strands, so the letters are woven into a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exam plus the old boy network turns out a very upper-class product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old boy network' reads as one phrase, but 'network' is the signal: a net weaves strands into a new pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristocrats are said to have blue blood, and the bloodline of kings and queens is the bluest of all.

clue.text: Depression? You need a holiday

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an alcove or hollow set back in a wall
second meaning: a break from work, as when Parliament adjourns

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests advice for someone low in spirits; depression is a physical hollow, not a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hollow or niche and a period when a legislature or school stops work.

clue.text: See 21
Saint of the weather changes direction following Western rat — it's not that simple

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the weather saint is placed behind the western rat

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for western
a heel is a cad, a rat
St Swithin's Day rain is said to set the weather for forty days

explanation.surface: Weather lore about St Swithin's Day turns out more complicated than it looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds the grid's two lights, the saint after the western rat; the enumeration's final word repeats the first, the reading turning back to 21.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels within wheels describes a complex situation of hidden motives and influences, far from simple.

clue.text: Tree with deposit on land

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
an ore deposit is a body of mineral in rock

explanation.surface: A tree stands on a mineral seam on dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on the shore or on dry land, as opposed to at sea.

clue.text: Hild wantonly embracing boy with more money than industry

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly and without restraint, so the letters are thrown about
to embrace is to hug, so the jumbled letters wrap around the boy

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A saintly abbess named Hild behaves wantonly with a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Hild is St Hilda of Whitby, which makes 'wantonly' a scandalous joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The idle rich are wealthy people who do not need to work, having money but no diligence.

clue.text: Greeting without unction to surgeon (male, English): then please may I do a census on the roads?

definitions.text: then please may I do a census on the roads?

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the greeting goes round the unction

parts.note: 'How do?' is a northern English greeting
unction is anointing with oil
a vet is an animal surgeon
he is the male pronoun
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A bluff greeting to a doctor, then a request to count traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside, so the greeting goes round the oil. Elizabeth Barrett Browning's sonnet continues 'Let me count the ways', which the census on the roads parodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's opening line is followed by 'Let me count the ways', and counting the ways is jokily a road traffic census.

clue.text: See 24
Unexciting study of poet

parts.note: dry means dull
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A dull study of a poet's work.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was the leading English poet of the Restoration and the first Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Space explorers in step backwards, rising in relation to electrical unit under 8

indicators.note: backwards means the combined letters are read from right to left
in puts the space explorers inside the word for a pace

parts.note: taken as written
NASA is the US space agency
re means concerning
the volt is the unit of electrical potential

explanation.surface: Astronauts walking in reverse, rising in relation to electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under 8' points to Wat Tyler at 8 down, the revolt's leader; the 1381 rising in England was led by him.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt is an uprising, and the 1381 rebellion of English labourers against poll taxes was a famous rising.
